log.msg: Skipped the usage.json/usage.jsonl refresh on purpose: my fence does not name those files, so the mastermind keeps the snapshot current. window.before is read from the existing snapshot (five_hour 0.0%).

URGENT for the owner: the repo root node_modules was EMPTY when I started. The dev server on port 80 (pid 9572) is only alive because it was started before that happened - it holds express in memory. Any restart (a Server/ save, a reboot, the supervisor's own watchdog) would have failed the boot test and the site would not have come back. I ran `npm ci` at the root (reads the existing package-lock.json, writes only the gitignored node_modules, edits no tracked file) - 70 packages in 550ms. `import('./Server/Server.js')` now resolves and the owner's site is still 200. Nobody needs to do anything; this line is the record of why node_modules changed.

AUDIT 1/4 - what the old Servex (C:/Code/servex/Servex/) actually does, and it is small: 4 files, 314 lines. Servex.js scans C:/Code one level deep, calls any directory with a package.json a Project, and gives each one a port. PortRegistry.js remembers name->port in a JSON file so a project keeps its port across restarts. ReverseProxy.js listens on 80, reads the Host header, strips `.localhost`, and forwards to that port - HTTP and WebSocket upgrades both. Its best idea is the one the plan did not call for: when the proxy gets ECONNREFUSED it starts the project and serves a small self-polling `Starting...` page, so visiting a stopped project's URL boots it. Project.js finds the start command (npm start, else server.js/index.js/app.js). pm2 does the actual spawning and the status events.

AUDIT 2/4 - what the monorepo Server/ already does that Servex must NOT rebuild. Server.js is the express+http base with an Events mixin (assign-based constructor, static `use(plugin)` on a `new` event) - that is the class Servex's dashboard extends. server.js at the repo root is a supervisor that boot-tests a changed child on a spare port and only promotes it on a real HTTP 200; that is strictly better than pm2's blind restart, and it stays the dev server's own business - Servex starts `node server.js` and lets the supervisor do its job inside. plugins/MCP.js is a hand-rolled Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint (one POST, one JSON answer, no SDK, no SSE, loopback-only) with a `register(tool, handler)` seam - copied and generalised, not imported. plugins/Whisper.js has the four boot cases worth keeping verbatim. Server/watch.js + MtimeFilter solve the Windows trap where merely READING a file fires a change event.

AUDIT 3/4 - the gaps servex-mvp.md names, and what I did about each. (a) ports.json sits in process.cwd() - moved to %LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/servex/ports.json. (b) everything binds 0.0.0.0 - every listener in the port binds 127.0.0.1. (c) scan root hardcoded to C:/Code - kept as the default but it is a constructor field you can assign. (d) no `bin` entry - left alone, distribution is not this phase. (e) the proxy hard-binds port 80 - now a configurable field, default 8080, because port 80 is the owner's. Two gaps the doc lists as unfixable here: Server is not npm-installable (its SPA fallback resolves index.html against its own package), and LiveReload never fires in Servex because SocketServer.setup hardcodes `new SocketServer(...)` instead of `new this(...)`. Both live in Server/, which is outside my fence - the second is a one-word fix and the mastermind should route it.

AUDIT 4/4 - the 09-19 servex-study said `rewrite small, not Servex, not pm2`; today's brief overrides the first half and I am keeping the second. Its case against pm2 holds and got stronger: pm2 is a SECOND always-on daemon under an always-on process, its crash-restart is blind where the monorepo supervisor's is boot-tested, and the study itself noted that merely running `pm2 -v` left an idle daemon behind. Servex supervises its children directly with child_process.spawn.

decision.question: How does Servex keep a child dev server alive - pm2, or its own spawn?
options: pm2 (what the old Servex used): a battle-tested process manager, start-at-login, per-process log files, a bus of status events - but it is a second always-on daemon running underneath an always-on process, its restart is blind (it will happily restart a broken build in a loop), and it is one more npm dependency and one more thing to install on a new machine.

Servex's own Process part, wrapping child_process.spawn: about 90 lines, restart-on-crash with an exponential backoff, PORT in the env, stdout/stderr lines going straight into our own log writer - no daemon, no dependency, and each child's own supervisor (node server.js boot-tests before it swaps) still does the smart part.
decision.chose: Servex's own Process part; no pm2.
decision.why: The brief asked for a concrete reason to use pm2 and there is not one. Servex IS the always-on process - a second daemon under it is one too many, and the handover already lists an idle pm2 daemon as clutter. Everything pm2 gave the old Servex (spawn with PORT, stop, status events) is under 90 lines here, and the two things pm2 would have added - blind crash-restart and per-process logs - we do better: the monorepo supervisor boot-tests a restart on a spare port before promoting it, and Log.js owns the log files as a single writer. Start-at-login is a real pm2 feature we give up; it is an OS integration (a scheduled task), not a reason to run a daemon.

decision.question: What port does the reverse proxy listen on?
options: Port 80, as the old Servex did - the prettiest URLs (monorepo.localhost with no port at all).
decision.why: Port 80 is the owner's own dev server and is in use right now (pid 9572). A field means the day Servex takes over from that server, the answer is `new Servex({ proxy_port: 80 })` and nothing else changes.

decision.question: Where do the port registry and the log files live?
options: In the repo, beside the code (servex.ports.json in cwd, as the old Servex did).
decision.why: The MVP doc lists the cwd file as its own open item: it breaks the moment Servex runs from anywhere but its own repo. It also keeps machine state out of git, which matters more here - log files grow without bound and a worktree would otherwise get its own copy of the port map and hand two projects the same port. Same home as Server/plugins/Whisper.js already uses (%LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/whisper), so there is one place to look.

decision.question: Servex's dashboard is a Server from ../Server/Server.js - but that class serves the monorepo's public/ and binds 0.0.0.0. How?
options: Import Server and configure it at the call site.
Subclass it and override the two methods that are wrong for Servex.
Write a separate small express server for Servex and not use Server at all.
decision.chose: Subclass: Servex.Dashboard extends Server, overriding initialize_express() (serve Servex/public/, SPA-fallback to Servex's own index.html) and listen() (bind 127.0.0.1).
decision.why: Server has no options for either - express.static("public") is cwd-relative and the SPA fallback resolves index.html against Server/'s own package, which is exactly the npm-installability gap servex-mvp.md names. The class is written to be subclassed (every method a seam), so overriding two methods costs eight lines and needs no change inside my fence-excluded Server/. Servex still eats its own cooking - it is the same Server every project here uses.

log.msg: DELIVERABLE 2 - Servex boots. `node Servex/index.js` from the repo root brings up one process with four parts: the dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8090 (a Servex.Dashboard extends Server, serving Servex/public/ with the monorepo's public/ behind it so the page can import the real View), the reverse proxy on 127.0.0.1:8080, the port registry at %LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/servex/ports.json, and the project list - 12 projects found under C:/Code at two levels deep, which is what it takes to find C:/Code/lew42/monorepo. Every listener binds 127.0.0.1 (the MVP doc's 0.0.0.0 gap), and there is a second lock on top: an express middleware refuses any non-loopback request to /api, /log and /mcp. No dependency was added - http-proxy and the Agent SDK were already in Servex/package.json.

DELIVERABLE 3 - supervision without pm2, and it is proven. `node Servex/proof.mjs` runs six checks and all six PASS: (1) restart() on an already-dead child spawns a fresh one in 3ms instead of waiting forever for an exit event that already happened - that exact wedge is the 2026-09-19 incident; (2) a child that exits on boot backs off 0.5s, 1s, 2s ... and gives up after 8 - measured 9 restarts in 1827ms, where a tight loop would be thousands; (3) a port held by a stranger is seen BEFORE spawning - status `port-taken`, nothing spawned; (4) a crash after a healthy run resets the backoff, so one crash a week later restarts instantly; (5) stop() takes the whole process tree - a grandchild's port was held before stop and free after, which matters because every dev server here is `node server.js`, a supervisor that forks the real server, and a plain child.kill() on Windows would leave it holding the port forever; (6) is the log proof below. Whisper is one of these processes: Process.Whisper handles the same four boot cases as Server/plugins/Whisper.js, and case 2 proved itself live on the first boot - `whisper-server is already answering on 127.0.0.1:8178 - leaving it alone`. Nothing was removed from the dev server's own Whisper plugin; a server started BY Servex gets NO_WHISPER=1 in its env, and the started server's own log line confirms it read it.

DELIVERABLE 4 - the single-writer log, proven. Servex/Log.js opens one write stream per file and keeps one promise chain per file, so line N+1 is not handed to the stream until line N is flushed. Proof 6: two SEPARATE OS processes each POSTed 200 entries to http://127.0.0.1:8090/log/<name>; the file came back with 400 lines in 192ms, 0 unparseable, and each poster's own 200 in the exact order it sent them. Log files live at %LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/servex/logs/<name>.jsonl. `at` is stamped by Servex in local time with its offset, the same format say.mjs writes. A log name is checked against a strict pattern before it becomes a filename - `/log/../../etc/passwd` is a request somebody can type.

DELIVERABLE 5 - /mcp, proven with a real claude turn. `claude -p --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config` pointed at http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp came back naming all six tools (list_servers, start_server, restart_server, stop_server, server_logs, append_log) and reading monorepo's port 3104 out of list_servers - a Haiku turn, 12.5s, $0.047, session f8494298-d2fb-4e6e-b975-351bc56fd1a0. The protocol shape is Server/plugins/MCP.js copied and emptied: one POST, one application/json answer, no session, no SSE, loopback-only. The seam the sibling agent-host task needs is `servex.mcp.tool(definition, handler)`, and it also accepts a definition carrying its own handler, so a module exporting a list registers with `for (const t of tools) servex.mcp.tool(t)`. Registering a name twice replaces it.

DELIVERABLE 6 - the end-to-end proof, in one gesture. With the monorepo STOPPED, a request to monorepo.localhost:8080/framework/ came back 200 with an X-Servex-Starting header and a self-polling page; two seconds later the same URL served the real site (2911 bytes, and /framework/framework.css alongside it). The started server logged `Server listening on 0.0.0.0:3104`, `[whisper] NO_WHISPER=1 -- skipping`, and its requests, all into monorepo.jsonl. restart_server and stop_server through the MCP then both worked: after restart the URL was 200 again, after stop port 3104 was free. The owner's own server on port 80 (pid 9572) was untouched throughout, checked before and after. I took the reload hold for the whole window because a second dev server rebuilds directory.json.

DELIVERABLE 7 - the dashboard page, measured at four widths headless. 11 project cards, no console errors, no failed requests, no horizontal overflow at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440. Page height 641px at 1280, 515 at 1920, 498 at 3440 - one screen at every width above a phone; 1978px at 400, which is the stacked one-column fallback. The first cut got this wrong and is worth recording: fixed-width cards in a flex wrap left about 800px of grey between the wall and the log panel at 1280. The fix was the layout skill's own rule - a grid of `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(13rem, 1fr))`, auto-fit rather than auto-fill because the project count is small and variable, with the floor in rem so it does not scale with the viewport type. The page uses the framework's real View layer (served from the monorepo's public/ as Servex's second static root) and its own 40 lines of servex- prefixed CSS; it does not load framework.css, because it is a standalone tool on its own origin rather than a page of the site.

FOR THE MASTERMIND - two things I could not fix from inside my fence, both in Server/. (1) `Server.listen` defaults to host 0.0.0.0, so a dev server Servex starts binds every interface even though Servex itself binds only 127.0.0.1; a one-line default change, or a `host` field read from the env, closes the last half of the MVP doc's 0.0.0.0 gap. (2) servex-mvp.md's LiveReload bug is still real: SocketServer.setup hardcodes `new SocketServer(...)` instead of `new this(...)`, so DevSocket.use(LiveReload) never reaches the constructed instance. One word. Neither blocks anything I built.

ask.topic: A one-line rule for CLAUDE.md - yours to add, not mine
ask.conclusion: The line, ready to paste under `## Ask before` or beside the dev-server note: **Claude sessions never start dev servers; Servex does** - `start_server` / `restart_server` / `stop_server` / `server_logs` on the Servex MCP at http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp (`Servex/readme.md`). CLAUDE.md is your own config, so I wrote the line instead of the file. It is worth having: today a session that wants a server starts one by hand, nobody records the PID, and the ports collide; with Servex running, every session asks the same process and the process remembers.

decision.question: Does the dashboard page load the site's framework (app.js, framework.css), or just the View layer?
options: The whole app.js - App, Router, Sidebar, DevBar, the lew42 theme. Consistent with the site, and every utility class works.
core/View/View.js alone, plus forty lines of the dashboard's own CSS.
decision.why: Servex's dashboard is a standalone tool on its own origin and its own port, not a page of the site - booting the site's Router and theme on it would make the tool depend on the thing it supervises, and drag in the whole @layer discipline for a single page. View is one import with one dependency (util/is) and gives the real factory API the old Servex page.js was written against. Adding App later is one line if the dashboard ever becomes a site page.

decision.question: How does the dashboard get live data - a WebSocket, or polling?
options: DevSocket, as the old Servex used, pushing projectStatus over a WebSocket.
Plain polling: /api/projects every 2s, the open log every 1.5s.
decision.why: Fewer parts, and the old Servex's own MVP doc notes its LiveReload never fired because of a bug in the shared SocketServer that is still unfixed and outside this task's fence. This is one person looking at one page on localhost; a socket would save bytes nobody is counting. The seam is a method (`logs()`, `projects()`), so swapping in a push later changes two functions.

decision.question: How does Servex start a project - `npm start`, or `node <entry>`?
options: npm start first, as the old Servex did - it respects whatever the project declared.
The entry file (server.js / index.js / app.js) with node, falling back to npm start.
decision.why: `npm start` is two processes, and on Windows the npm one is a .cmd that modern Node refuses to spawn without a shell, so it is really three - and a tree three deep is how a port ends up held by a process nobody can find. `node server.js` is also exactly what this monorepo wants (its root package.json has no start script at all) and it puts PORT where the server reads it. npm start is still the fallback, with shell: true.

assign.outcome:
**Servex is ported, it runs, and one command starts everything.** `node Servex/index.js` from the repo root brings up a dashboard, a reverse proxy, the port registry and the project list in a single process — and from now on a Claude session asks Servex for a dev server instead of starting one itself.

The headline proof: with the monorepo **stopped**, a request to `monorepo.localhost:8080/framework/` came back with a self-polling "Starting…" page, and two seconds later the same URL served the real site. Start, restart and stop all work through the MCP too. Your own server on port 80 was never touched, and neither was the whisper-server already running on 8178 — Servex only ever stops a process it started.

**Read first: `Servex/readme.md`** — one screen: the three URLs, the four parts, where the log and port files live, and the seam for adding MCP tools. It sits beside `Server/` in the repo, so open it in the editor; Servex is not served by the site.

**All eight deliverables are proven.**

1. **The audit** — five log lines below: what the old Servex does that works, what this monorepo's `Server/` already does better (the boot-tested supervisor, the MCP shape, Whisper's four boot cases), and each gap `servex-mvp.md` names with what I did about it.
2. **It boots** — 12 projects found two levels deep under `C:/Code`, which is what it takes to find the monorepo. Every listener binds `127.0.0.1`, and a middleware refuses any non-loopback caller on top of that. No new dependency.
3. **Supervision without pm2** — `node Servex/proof.mjs`, six checks, all PASS: restart on an already-dead child (3ms, no wait-forever — that exact wedge is the 2026-09-19 incident), a crash loop backing off and giving up after 8, a port held by a stranger caught before spawning, a backoff that resets after a healthy run, and `stop()` taking the whole process tree (every dev server here is `node server.js`, a supervisor that forks the real server). Whisper is one of these processes.
4. **The single-writer log** — two separate OS processes, 200 appends each through Servex's HTTP door: 400 lines in 192ms, none unparseable, each poster's own 200 in order.
5. **`/mcp`** — proven with a real `claude -p` turn that listed all six tools and read the monorepo's port out of `list_servers`. The seam for the sibling `agent-host` task is `servex.mcp.tool(definition, handler)`, documented in the readme.
6. **End to end** — the headline above.
7. **readme + dashboard** — the dashboard measured at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440: no console errors, no failed requests, no overflow, and one screen (641px tall at 1280) at every width above a phone.
8. **The CLAUDE.md line** is written as an `ask` below — it is your file, so I did not touch it. One minute to paste.

**One thing you should know:** the repo's root `node_modules` was **empty** when I started. Your dev server on port 80 was alive only because it had loaded express before that happened — any restart would have failed its boot test and the site would not have come back. I ran `npm ci` (lockfile only, no tracked file changed) and it is fixed. Nothing for you to do.

**Left, with reasons.** Two fixes live in `Server/`, outside my fence, and neither blocks anything: `Server.listen` still defaults to host `0.0.0.0`, so a dev server Servex starts binds every interface even though Servex does not; and `SocketServer.setup` hardcodes `new SocketServer(...)` instead of `new this(...)`, the one-word bug that has kept LiveReload from ever firing in Servex. No screenshot is attached because the task dir is under `public/`, which my fence made read-only apart from this log.

Every process I started is dead: Servex was pid 10312, killed with its tree; ports 8080, 8090 and 3104 are all free. Bringing it back is one command.
